routes.local_title: Pólya–Szegő conjecture for the first buckling load
routes.source_abstract: Lean formalization proving the planar Polya-Szego conjecture for the first buckling eigenvalue. For open planar sets of positive finite area, it proves the sharp area inequality and characterizes equality by exact equality with an open disk. It retains the original Sobolev-space, variational eigenvalue and Bessel definitions, and includes the disk eigenvalue and buckling–Dirichlet comparison.

routes.source_title: Dimension-free KLS Poincare bound for isotropic log-concave densities (smooth compactly supported tests)
routes.source_abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib library for Poincare inequalities, log-concave probability measures and stochastic localization. Its dimension-free KLS theorem bounds the intrinsic local-slope Poincare constant by one universal constant times the covariance operator norm, including dimension zero and singular affine supports, for log-concave probability laws with finite second moment. The proof follows Bizeul-Klartag-Lehec through finite-horizon cutoff localization, the compact Letwin constant-8 quadratic variance bound and approximation. Supporting results include Cheeger-Buser comparisons, covariance and energy interfaces and moment-map calculus. This entry checks the pinned OpenAI density formulation: for every n >= 1 and isotropic measurable log-concave probability density, Var(f) <= C * E|grad f|^2 for every smooth compactly supported real test, with one positive C before all dimensions and laws. No numerical final KLS constant, formal equivalence with the paper's locally Lipschitz L^2 test class, or uncut Eldan construction is claimed.

routes.local_title: Finiteness of planar central configurations for fixed masses
routes.source_title: Finiteness of Planar Central Configurations for Five Positive Masses
routes.source_abstract: We prove that, for any five positive masses, there are finitely many planar Newtonian central configurations up to translations, rotations, and positive scaling. Building on the singular-diagram framework of Albouy and Kaloshin, we treat the exceptional masses left open by their finiteness theorem. The proof retains a lower bound for the physical potential after passing to the complex algebraic equations. On each fixed potential level, energy estimates, torque identities, and local response calculations control the possible degenerations. A polynomial selection argument then yields finiteness. The exceptional local calculations and their algebraic certificates are given explicitly. A separate Lean development accompanies the proof.

routes.local_title: Does the disk minimize the third Dirichlet eigenvalue?
routes.source_title: The fourth consecutive Dirichlet eigenvalue ratio
routes.source_abstract: An unconditional Lean proof of the strict inequality lambda_5 / lambda_4 < C_N for every nonempty bounded connected open subset of Euclidean space of dimension at least two, with variational Dirichlet eigenvalues and the sharp Bessel-zero constant. No boundary regularity is assumed.

routes.local_title: Beat factor two for scheduling on unrelated machines
routes.source_title: Graham's bounds for list scheduling and LPT on identical machines: 2 − 1/m, 4/3 − 1/(3m) and their tight instances
routes.source_abstract: A Lean 4 development of Graham's two bounds for scheduling independent jobs on identical machines to minimize the makespan (R. L. Graham, Bounds for certain multiprocessing anomalies, Bell System Tech. J. 45 (1966) 1563-1581; Bounds on multiprocessing timing anomalies, SIAM J. Appl. Math. 17 (1969) 416-429; both restated with their examples in his survey Bounds on multiprocessing anomalies and related packing algorithms, AFIPS Spring Joint Computer Conference (1972) 205-217). n jobs of nonnegative real lengths p : Fin n -> R are run without interruption on m >= 1 identical machines; an assignment sigma : Fin n -> Fin m loads machine i with the sum of the lengths assigned to it, its makespan is the largest load, and optMakespan m p is the least makespan over all m^n assignments. A list schedule (IsListSchedule, in the index order) gives each job a machine whose load from the earlier jobs is least, under any tie-breaking (a relation, so every theorem covers every tie-breaking); an LPT schedule (IsLPTSchedule) is a list schedule of the jobs in some nonincreasing order of length. Theorems, kernel-only: every list schedule sigma and every assignment tau satisfy m * C(sigma) <= (2m - 1) * C(tau) (Graham 1966, his Theorem for the same number of processors and no precedence constraints), so C(sigma) <= (2 - 1/m) * optMakespan; the m(m - 1) unit jobs followed by one job of length m (Graham's example for his theorem on scheduling the k largest tasks optimally first, at k = 0, as his 1972 survey restates it; Lenstra-Shmoys, Chapter 9, p. 188) have optimum m and every list schedule of them in that order has makespan 2m - 1, so 2 - 1/m is the least constant (IsLeast); every LPT schedule sigma and every assignment tau satisfy 3m * C(sigma) <= (4m - 1) * C(tau) (Graham 1969, Theorem 2, announced in the closing remarks of the 1966 paper), so C(sigma) <= (4/3 - 1/(3m)) * optMakespan; when every job is longer than a third of C(tau), every LPT schedule is at least as good as tau, so LPT is optimal when every job exceeds a third of the optimum; Graham's 2m + 1 jobs 2m - 1, 2m - 1, 2m - 2, 2m - 2, ..., m + 1, m + 1, m, m, m (his pp. 425-426) are in nonincreasing order, have optimum 3m, attained by a list schedule in the order 2m - 1, ..., m + 1, m, m, 2m - 1, ..., m + 1, m (the definition grahamOrder, a permutation of the jobs whose lengths are that list), and every LPT schedule of them has makespan 4m - 1, for every m >= 1, so 4/3 - 1/(3m) is the least constant (IsLeast); and the elementary facts (list and LPT schedules exist, the optimum is attained, every load, every job and the average load are at most the makespan, relabeling the jobs preserves the makespan); Graham's omega_0, the least finishing time over all lists, equals the optimum over all assignments (every assignment is matched or improved by a list schedule in some order), so the bounds against every assignment are his; for his instance the optimum is attained by an explicit list (grahamOrder); and the third of the optimality theorem cannot be weakened (on three machines 9, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, each job at least a third of the optimum 12, has an LPT schedule of makespan 13, so n <= 2m jobs do not make LPT optimal; Graham's 1972 survey prints Spencer's 6, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2 for the same purpose); and the position of a job on its machine: the (c + 1)-th job k placed on a machine of a list schedule of a nonincreasing p has (c + 1) p_k <= C(tau) for every assignment tau (the property of Chen 1993, as Della Croce-Scatamacchia 2020 restate it; proved here by an invariant on pairs of machines), hence the Coffman-Sethi form q m C(sigma) <= ((q + 1) m - 1) C(tau) for a machine with q jobs attaining the makespan of an LPT schedule (Coffman-Sethi 1976 as corrected by Chen 1993, as Della Croce-Scatamacchia restate it; the literature states it for q >= 3, for m >= 2 it is weaker than the 4/3 - 1/(3m) bound at q <= 2, and neither its attainment nor Chen's 4/3 - 1/(3(m - 1)) at q = 2 is proved here; Chen's and Coffman-Sethi's papers were not read). The proof of the LPT bound is by counting, not by his exchange argument: with k the job ending a heaviest machine, the average-load bound settles 3 p_k <= C(tau), and otherwise a count of the jobs up to k (every machine of tau holds at most two of them, those at least as long as the least load sit alone, each single-job machine of sigma contributes one) shows that k's machine ends by C(tau). Further: for a job k completing at the makespan of a list schedule of a nonincreasing p, the smaller of C(sigma) and 3 p_k is at most C(tau) for every tau, and C(sigma) <= 3 p_k certifies optimality; equality 3m C(sigma) = (4m - 1) C(tau) on m >= 2 machines forces 3 p_k = C(tau), equal loads before k, every load of tau equal to C(tau) and no positive job after k; Della Croce-Scatamacchia's Proposition 4, q (m - 1) C(sigma) <= ((q + 1)(m - 1) - 1) C(tau) when another machine holds q jobs before k and q + 2 <= m, proved from Chen's property; Dósa's theorem (2004, Theorem 2: Graham's example is the only tight one): every positive multiple of Graham's 2m + 1 jobs in any order attains the bound, and for a nonempty positive instance on m >= 2 machines a list schedule in nonincreasing order, or an LPT schedule in any order, attains 3m C(sigma) = (4m - 1) optMakespan only when the instance is a positive multiple of Graham's jobs, so the inequality is strict for every number of jobs other than 2m + 1; and for every fixed n >= 2m + 1 the constant 4/3 - 1/(3m) is the supremum (IsLUB) of C(sigma)/optMakespan over the LPT schedules of the positive instances with n jobs (the proof approaches it with Graham's jobs followed by small jobs; Dósa's Remark 1 asserts a strict gap for every n != 2m + 1, which can therefore hold at most for n < 2m + 1, not formalized here). Forty-one compared statements over nine fully specified definitions; the finite facts behind every statement are replayed exactly in the standard library by scripts/check_lpt.py. As of 2026-10-11 no kernel-checked proof of the 4/3 - 1/(3m) bound, of either equality family or of the optimality statement was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, anthropics/formal-math, the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index, GitHub code search in Lean or arXiv; the AFP's Approximation_Algorithms proves a 3/2 bound for sorted greedy and the factor 2 for greedy, and two Lean repositories prove m * C <= sum p + (m - 1) * p_max over lists of naturals. No priority is claimed.

routes.local_title: The exact asymptotic match fraction for independent binary sequences
routes.source_title: Upper bounds for the Chvátal–Sankoff constants $\gamma_k$, $k\ge3$
routes.source_abstract: Lueker (J. ACM 56(3), 2009) constructed a family of finite-state machines $\mathcal{M}_h$ whose associated transfer matrices yield upper bounds on the Chvátal–Sankoff constants $\gamma_k$, and proved (his Theorem 3.26) that these bounds converge to $\gamma_k$ for every alphabet size $k$. He published values only for $k=2$. For $k\ge3$ the best upper bounds we were able to find in the literature in September 2026 were still those of Dančík's 1994 thesis: subsequent work generalising Lueker has generalised his Section 2, the lower bound. We implement $\mathcal{M}_h$ for arbitrary $k$. One ingredient has no binary analogue — the generating function of a truncation class when both sides of a minimal match pair are truncated — and we derive it. We then give a reduction by relative forms under which the transition multiplicities of the transfer matrix are falling factorials in $k$; one alphabet-free construction consequently determines the exact matrix for every $k$. We obtain improved upper bounds for $k=3,\dots,15$, each supported by a Collatz–Wielandt certificate verified in exact rational arithmetic, among them $\gamma_5\le0.645033$. A note added on 31 October 2026 compares these values with those of a repository made public by L. Jack on 25 October 2026.

routes.local_title: The densest packing of congruent regular tetrahedra
routes.source_title: Densest packings of two translates of a lattice in five dimensions
routes.source_abstract: We prove that no packing of unit balls in $\R^5$ whose centres form two translates of a lattice is denser than the $D_5$ lattice packing. Up to congruence exactly three such packings attain this density: $\sqrt2\,D_5$, a layered packing of Leech, and the packing with Szöllősi's kissing configuration.

routes.source_title: LeanMMBound: the matrix multiplication exponent is below 2.3710449
routes.source_abstract: The matrix multiplication exponent ω is the least exponent such that n×n matrices can be multiplied in n^(ω+o(1)) operations. This repository proves in Lean 4 / Mathlib that ω < 2.3710449 over every commutative ring, improving the previous bound ω < 2.371177 (Dupont et al. 2026). ω is defined via the exact tensor rank of n×n matrix multiplication. The new ingredient is shared extraction across recursion levels of the asymmetric laser method. The formalization covers the full argument, from the Coppersmith–Winograd degeneration to an exact rational certificate checked in the Lean kernel. The construction and proof were produced largely by AI systems under the authors' direction.

An independent Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of a supplied bordered block-circulant sign matrix of order 668.  The main theorem proves that there exists a 668 by 668 integer matrix with entries in {-1, 1}, diagonal row norm 668, and zero inner product between every pair of distinct rows. The formalization is a certificate-specific existence result, not a classification of Hadamard matrices and not a proof of the general Hadamard conjecture.

routes.source_title: Matrix multiplication: omega at most 9/4 over every ring
routes.source_abstract: An integral extension of OpenAI's matrix multiplication exponent bound and its previous all-fields extension. The formalization proves that the exact integer coefficient tensor-rank exponent is at most 9/4, yielding division-free arithmetic programs over every associative unital ring, including noncommutative rings. For every positive epsilon, one constant bounds the operation count at all positive matrix sizes by C*n^(9/4+epsilon). The arithmetic model is preserved apart from Field-to-Ring assumptions. The extension uses a primitive tensor spectrum, coefficient extraction, fixed finite-free descent, and coprime patching of Fourier and interpolation constructions. It does not improve the numerical exponent or assert an endpoint O(n^(9/4)) algorithm, efficient uniform generation, or bit complexity.

routes.local_title: The exact minimum ropelength of a trefoil
routes.source_title: A certified upper bound for the distortion of the trefoil knot
routes.source_abstract: The distortion of a rectifiable closed curve $\gamma\subset\mathbb R^3$ is the supremum, over pairs of distinct points, of the ratio of the length of the shorter arc of $\gamma$ between them to their distance; the distortion $\delta(K)$ of a knot type $K$ is the infimum over all curves of type $K$. For the trefoil, the published lower bound is $\delta\ge5\pi/3$, valid for every non-trivial knot (a recent preprint claims $\delta>6.5321$), and the only upper bound we found in the literature is the value $7.16$ obtained by numerical simulation. We exhibit an explicit polygon with $192$ vertices, of knot type trefoil, whose distortion is at most $6.92$. The proof is computer-assisted: the knot type is certified by an explicit piecewise-linear path of embedded polygons starting from a polygon on a torus, and the distortion by exact rational arithmetic on every pair of edges. Two separately written verifiers are supplied.

routes.local_title: Polynomial mixing of planar Ising dynamics with plus boundary
routes.source_title: Lower and Upper Bounds for Glauber Dynamics from Typical States of the Low-Temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick Model
routes.source_abstract:
We study the heat-bath (Glauber) dynamics of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model at zero external field and fixed inverse temperature $\beta>1$. We sample the disorder $J$ and an initial configuration $X_0$ from its Gibbs measure. Let $T^J(X_0)$ be the time at which the transition law, conditional on $J$ and the realized $X_0$, first comes within total-variation distance $1/4$ of equilibrium. In continuous time, with rate one per site, we prove that, for every fixed $\omega\in(0,1/4)$, with probability tending to one,
\[
A_\beta n^{7/30}<\log T^J(X_0)\le n^{1-\omega},
\]
where $A_\beta>0$ depends only on $\beta$. Corresponding bounds hold for the discrete-time chain.

These results strengthen OpenAI’s typical-start lower and upper bounds while following their proof architectures. The lower-bound argument introduces a three-replica comparison with a cubic pressure deficit and uses Aronow and Lopatto’s quantitative mean-bias estimate. The upper-bound argument combines a pathwise information–energy cancellation, concentration estimates on a growing mesh, and optimized exponents.

We also complete Lean formalizations of two known results: OpenAI’s fluctuation-scale theorem, giving variance $n^{1/3+o(1)}$ for the log partition function, and its mean-bias consequence of order at least $n^{-5/6-\varepsilon}$ for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. The formal development proves the positive-Laplace-window input needed for the fluctuation theorem. Five specified result groups are formalized, including the continuous-time dynamics upper bound.

routes.source_title: Improved basis-change transformations for $2 \times 2$ matrix multiplication
routes.source_abstract:
To the best of our knowledge, we present a state-of-the-art change-of-basis algorithm for $2 \times 2$ matrix multiplication under the Karstadt--Schwartz-style basis change regime [1].
We do this by introducing basis-change matrices $B_U$, $B_V$, and $B_W$ that each require only a single addition and hence give rise to a matrix-multiplication algorithm performing $5n^{\log_2{7}} - 4n^2 + \frac{3}{4}n^2 \log_2{n},$ arithmetic operations when multiplying two $n \times n$ matrices, with $n$ a power of $2$. This improves on the previous best bound, which had last term $\frac{3}{2}n^2\log_2{n}$.

routes.source_title: Strict Neumann Polya inequality on simply connected planar domains
routes.source_abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the strict Neumann Pólya inequality for bounded simply connected Lipschitz domains in the plane. The plane is identified with ℂ; the Neumann eigenvalues μ_0 ≤ μ_1 ≤ ... are defined by the Courant–Fischer min–max formula for the form ∫|∇u|² on H¹(Ω) (weak gradients in L²), indexed from 0 and repeated according to multiplicity, and N_N(E) = #{j ≥ 0 : μ_j < E}. The principal results are: for every bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain Ω and every integer j ≥ 1, |Ω| μ_j(Ω) < 4πj; and, equivalently, N_N(E) > |Ω| E / (4π) for every E > 0. The proof development (about 100,000 lines, namespace PolyaNeumann) also identifies the variational eigenvalues with the spectrum of the constructed self-adjoint Neumann operator, proves a quantitative smooth-domain estimate via boundary transport, Cayley/monodromy rank bounds and a Herglotz-wave reduction, and passes to Lipschitz domains by smooth approximation.

routes.local_title: Bareket's conjecture for simply connected planar domains
routes.source_title: Strict Dirichlet Pólya inequality on simply connected planar domains
routes.source_abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the strict Dirichlet Pólya inequality for bounded, open, simply connected planar domains, including the indexed eigenvalue and counting formulations.

routes.local_title: Optimal spectral signings of regular graphs
routes.source_title: An explicit periodic signing of C_n(1,2) below the conjectured minimum
routes.source_abstract: The paper's disproof of Suvagiya's signed-circulant minimum conjecture on an infinite arithmetic progression, formalized at the matrix level. For every n divisible by 8, Lean defines the paper's period-8 triangle-flux signing of the circulant graph C_n(1,2) as an explicit signed adjacency matrix, proves it is a plus-minus-one signing of mathlib's circulant graph, and proves by exact rational sum-of-squares window certificates that every eigenvalue has absolute value at most 1397/500. For every n >= 32 this rational separator lies strictly below the conjectured minimum rho_-(n) = 2*sqrt(cos^2(pi/n)+cos^2(2pi/n)), so the conjectured value is beaten by an explicit signing on all of n = 0 mod 8, n >= 32. The full Bloch determinant identity and the all-phase algebraic band-edge certificate remain selected as the supporting layer.

routes.source_title: On the tightness of the Parthasarathy and Schmidt rank bounds for extremal tracial couplings
routes.source_abstract:
Let $2 \le a \le b$, and let $\rho_A, \rho_B$ be density operators on $\C^a$ and $\C^b$, respectively. Let
$\mathcal{C}(\rho_A, \rho_B)$ denote the set of bipartite couplings on $\C^a \otimes \C^b$ with these
marginals. Parthasarathy showed that every extreme coupling has rank at most
$\KRP(a,b) := \lfloor\sqrt{a^2+b^2-1}\rfloor$. It is not known for which dimension pairs $(a, b)$ this bound is tight.

We restrict attention to the tracial case $\rho_A = I_a/a$, $\rho_B = I_b/b$. For the Parthasarathy bound, we construct extreme couplings of rank $r$ from pairs of length-$r$ finite unit-norm tight frames (FUNTFs) in $\C^a$ and $\C^b$ satisfying a transversality condition. This yields an extreme coupling of rank $b$ for every $2 \le a < b$, and hence tightness of $\KRP(a,b)$ whenever $a<b$ and $b\ge(a^2-1)/2$; in particular, along the whole qubit-qudit line $(2,b)$, $b\ge3$. This recovers the two previously known tracial cases with $a<b$, namely $(2,3)$ and $(3,4)$.

The Schmidt decomposition and subadditivity of rank give the lower bound $\ES(a, b) := \lceil b/a\rceil$ for the rank of every tracial coupling, extreme or not. For the Schmidt bound, we use sparse Kraus operators built from weighted partial permutation matrices. Setting $r := \ES(a, b)$, we construct an extreme coupling of rank $r$ whenever $b-(r-1)a$ divides $a$, and show that for $a<b \le 2a$, where this condition reads $b-a=\gcd(a,b)$, it is also necessary. For $b>a(a-1)$, the divisibility condition is superfluous and the Schmidt bound is attained for every such $b$. Thus, for each fixed $a$, attainability of both bounds remains open for only finitely many $b\ge a$.
